content.text:
Below is the practical answer for **a Master’s degree obtained outside the EU/EEA** when you live in the **Brussels-Capital Region** and want to work in Brussels.

## 1) Is official recognition/equivalence always mandatory to work in Brussels?

**No. It is not always mandatory.** It depends on the job and the employer.

- For many **private-sector, non-regulated jobs**, an official equivalence is **generally not required**; the employer may assess your foreign Master’s themselves. The Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles says equivalence can be useful for job search, is necessary where the job requires a Belgian diploma, but is generally not necessary for private-sector work. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Actiris** similarly states that in the private sector equivalence is **not always necessary**, but that it will be requested for the **public sector** or publicly subsidised institutions. ([actiris.brussels](https://www.actiris.brussels/fr/citoyens/equivalence-de-mes-diplomes/))  
- For **regulated professions** — e.g. many health professions, teaching, lawyer, pharmacist, nurse, doctor, etc. — recognition is needed because access to the profession is legally conditional on holding a recognised title/qualification. FPS Economy’s Be-Assist page states that recognition of professional qualifications is necessary if you want to work in a **regulated profession**; if the profession is not regulated in the host state, you can practise it freely. ([economie.fgov.be](https://economie.fgov.be/en/themes/enterprises/starting-business/conditions-entering/be-assist/frequently-asked-questions-be))  

So the key question is not simply “Do I have a foreign Master’s?” but: **What job/profession do you want to do, and does the employer or law require a Belgian/recognised diploma?**

---

## 2) Which authority is competent for Brussels, and how does the choice work?

Brussels is bilingual and institutionally linked to both the **French Community / Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles** and the **Flemish Community**. For diploma recognition for work in Brussels, the two main routes are:

### A. Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles — French-language route

For higher-education diplomas, the competent service is the **Service de la reconnaissance académique et professionnelle des diplômes étrangers d’enseignement supérieur** of the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles. FPS Economy lists this French Community service as one of the community authorities to contact for a certificate/equivalence of a diploma for professional qualification recognition. ([economie.fgov.be](https://economie.fgov.be/en/themes/enterprises/starting-business/conditions-entering/be-assist/frequently-asked-questions-be))  

The FWB procedure concerns academic recognition/equivalence of foreign higher-education studies with FWB higher education. FWB distinguishes between **equivalence to a specific academic degree** and **equivalence of level** — for example, recognition that your diploma corresponds to Master’s level. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))  

### B. NARIC-Vlaanderen — Dutch-language / Flemish route

For work in Flanders or Brussels, the Flemish authority is **NARIC-Vlaanderen**. The official Flanders page states that if you want to work in **Flanders or Brussels** with a foreign diploma, you may have to get it recognised, and the NARIC-Vlaanderen application wizard helps determine whether/where you need to apply. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/recognition-and-equivalence-of-a-foreign-diploma-or-certificate-in-flanders))  

NARIC-Vlaanderen states that if you have a foreign diploma and are going to work in **Flanders or Brussels**, in many cases you need recognition, and in most cases NARIC-Vlaanderen is the competent authority. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/working-enterprise-and-investment/working/working-in-flanders-with-a-foreign-diploma/applying-for-recognition-of-equivalence-of-your-diploma-by-naric-vlaanderen?utm_source=openai))  

### How to choose in Brussels

For a Brussels job, the practical choice often depends on the **language/community link of the employer or the job**:

- If the employer or vacancy is linked to the **French-speaking sector**, use the **Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles** route.
- If the employer or vacancy is linked to the **Dutch-speaking/Flemish sector**, use **NARIC-Vlaanderen**.
- If the employer is **bilingual Dutch/French**, NARIC-Vlaanderen says you may apply either to NARIC-Vlaanderen or to the French Community NARIC centre, and you should ask the future employer which they prefer. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/recognition-and-equivalence-of-a-foreign-diploma-or-certificate-in-flanders))  
- The Brussels-Capital Region’s own information page directs people to both French Community and Flemish Community/NARIC-Vlaanderen sources for diploma equivalence. ([be.brussels](https://be.brussels/en/education-teaching/equivalence-diplomas))  

**Practical tip:** before applying, ask the employer or the job-selection service:  
> “Do you require recognition by FWB, by NARIC-Vlaanderen, or either?”

That can save time and money.

---

## 3) How the concepts and procedures differ by job type

### A. Non-regulated private-sector job

Examples: many business, IT, marketing, project-management, finance, research, NGO, communications or administrative roles where the law does not reserve the profession to holders of a specific Belgian title.

For this category:

- **Official equivalence is usually not legally mandatory.** The employer may decide whether your foreign Master’s is acceptable.
- An equivalence can still be useful if the employer wants proof that your foreign degree is at Belgian/Flemish/FWB **Master’s level**.
- In the FWB system, a **level equivalence** can legally establish the level of your studies — for example Master’s level — but it does **not** assess the detailed content or give access to jobs requiring a specific diploma. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))  
- In the Flemish/NARIC system, the guidance tool indicates which type of recognition you can apply for, including **level recognition** or **specific recognition**. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/working-enterprise-and-investment/working/working-in-flanders-with-a-foreign-diploma/applying-for-recognition-of-equivalence-of-your-diploma-by-naric-vlaanderen?utm_source=openai))  

For a non-regulated private-sector job, the most common need — if any — is therefore a **level recognition** showing that your foreign diploma corresponds to a Belgian/Flemish/FWB higher-education level, such as Master’s level.

### B. Public-sector job or publicly subsidised institution

Examples: a job with a commune, regional administration, federal administration, school network, public hospital, public agency, or institution subsidised by public authorities.

For this category:

- Equivalence is much more likely to be required.
- Actiris states that if you want to work in the **public sector** or in an institution subsidised by public authorities, an equivalence of your diploma will be requested. ([actiris.brussels](https://www.actiris.brussels/fr/citoyens/equivalence-de-mes-diplomes/))  
- FWB similarly says that if you want to work in the public sector or in a publicly subsidised institution, you will likely have to request recognition of your diploma. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))  

The exact type of equivalence depends on the vacancy:

- If the vacancy requires “a Master’s degree” generally, a **level equivalence** may be enough.
- If it requires a specific Belgian/FWB/Flemish diploma — for example “Master in law,” “Master in psychology,” “Master in engineering,” etc. — the employer may require **specific equivalence** to that academic degree.

Always check the wording of the job notice.

### C. Regulated profession

A **regulated profession** is one where access to or exercise of the profession is subject to legal conditions — often a specific diploma, professional title, registration, licence, professional body approval, visa, or authorisation.

For this category:

- Recognition is **not just useful**; it is normally required because the law controls access to the profession.
- FPS Economy states that professional-qualification recognition is necessary if you want to work in a regulated profession; if the profession is not regulated, you can practise it freely. ([economie.fgov.be](https://economie.fgov.be/en/themes/enterprises/starting-business/conditions-entering/be-assist/frequently-asked-questions-be))  
- FWB explains that a **level equivalence** does not give access to jobs requiring a specific diploma, especially regulated professions such as nurse, doctor, pharmacist or lawyer. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))  
- NARIC-Vlaanderen warns that for certain professions you must apply to an organisation other than NARIC-Vlaanderen, including healthcare professions, teaching professions or other regulated professions in Flanders/Brussels. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/recognition-and-equivalence-of-a-foreign-diploma-or-certificate-in-flanders))  

For a **non-EU/EEA diploma**, the professional route can be more complex. FPS Economy’s Be-Assist page explains that EU Directive 2005/36/EC mainly concerns professional qualifications within the EU/EEA framework; for qualifications obtained in a third country, the first recognition is generally under national rules, and third-country nationals do not generally fall within the Directive unless a special equal-treatment situation applies. ([economie.fgov.be](https://economie.fgov.be/en/themes/enterprises/starting-business/conditions-entering/be-assist/frequently-asked-questions-be))  

In practice, for regulated professions you often need one or more of the following:

1. **Academic equivalence** of the diploma — often specific, not merely level-based.
2. **Professional recognition or authorisation** by the competent professional authority.
3. **Registration/visa/licence** where applicable.
4. Possibly proof of language knowledge, traineeship, adaptation period, aptitude test, or additional training.

The competent authority depends on the profession — for example health, education, legal, accounting, architecture, real-estate, etc. NARIC/FWB can tell you whether your case remains an academic-equivalence matter or must go to a sector-specific authority.

---

## 4) Current official sources supporting this answer

The main official sources are:

1. **Brussels-Capital Region — “Equivalence of diplomas”**  
   This page refers Brussels residents to Belgium.be, MyDiploma, the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles equivalence services, and NARIC-Vlaanderen for diploma recognition information. ([be.brussels](https://be.brussels/en/education-teaching/equivalence-diplomas))  

2. **Actiris — “Équivalence de mes diplômes”**  
   Actiris explains what diploma equivalence is, when recognition is needed, and states that private-sector equivalence is not always necessary while public-sector or publicly subsidised jobs generally request it. ([actiris.brussels](https://www.actiris.brussels/fr/citoyens/equivalence-de-mes-diplomes/))  

3. **Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles — higher-education diploma equivalence**  
   FWB explains that academic recognition/equivalence compares foreign higher-education studies with FWB higher education; it distinguishes **specific academic-degree equivalence** from **level equivalence**, and notes that private-sector equivalence is generally not necessary while regulated professions/public-sector contexts may require it. ([equisup.cfwb.be](https://equisup.cfwb.be/equivalence/quest-ce-quune-equivalence/?utm_source=openai))  

4. **NARIC-Vlaanderen / Flanders.be — recognition of foreign diplomas for work in Flanders or Brussels**  
   NARIC-Vlaanderen explains that people who want to work in Flanders or Brussels may need recognition, that the application wizard helps determine whether/where to apply, and that for bilingual employers in Brussels either NARIC-Vlaanderen or the French Community NARIC centre may be acceptable depending on employer preference. ([vlaanderen.be](https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/recognition-and-equivalence-of-a-foreign-diploma-or-certificate-in-flanders))  

5. **FPS Economy — Be-Assist / professional qualifications**  
   This official Belgian source explains regulated professions, the difference between regulated and non-regulated professions, and the specific issues for third-country qualifications and third-country nationals under professional-qualification recognition rules. ([economie.fgov.be](https://economie.fgov.be/en/themes/enterprises/starting-business/conditions-entering/be-assist/frequently-asked-questions-be))  

**Bottom line:** for a Master’s obtained outside the EU/EEA, do not automatically apply blindly. First identify whether the Brussels job is **non-regulated private-sector**, **public-sector/subsidised**, or a **regulated profession**; then ask the employer or competent professional body whether they require FWB recognition, NARIC-Vlaanderen recognition, or sector-specific professional recognition.
